catalog.description: Parking share lets whoever holds a parking space offer it for a period when they will not use it, and lets a neighbour claim it. Somebody who needs a space can post a wanted ad with the days and a short note, and a holder can reply to it or reserve their space for them. The board assigns each space, sees every offer, claim, wanted ad and reply, and can remove an ad or a reply. Besides residents, the board can let board members who live elsewhere, the administrator, the property manager and people it gives access, such as somebody who rents a garage, use the module. Everybody who uses it, except the board, sees a space and its days, and a wanted ad's days and note, but not who is behind them unless that person chooses to show it. The board sees every name. The module mails confirmations, mails a poster about replies, reservations, and the removal of their ad or of a reply to it, and mails a holder whose reply the board removes. It handles no payment. Offers and claims are erased a year after the period they cover, and wanted ads and their replies 30 days after the ad's last day. The board's assignment of a space is kept for up to five years, or until the board removes it. The module rests on the association's legitimate interest, so anybody can object to it; once the board grants the objection, the module no longer sees them and they can no longer use it. Two things to tell residents: an offer shows that a space is free on certain days, so a neighbour who knows whose space it is can tell the household is away; and everybody who uses the module, the property manager included, reads the note on a wanted ad, so it should not name anybody else.
